title: My Parents Kept the Basement Locked for 18 Years. On My Birthday, I Went In.
hook: My parents kept ONE door locked for 18 years…
story: Growing up, my house had one locked door: the basement. Every birthday, I'd ask what was down there, and every birthday my parents would say, "When you're eighteen." So on my eighteenth birthday, my dad handed me a key, and he couldn't stop smiling. I walked down those stairs expecting something terrible. The lights flickered on, and the walls were covered, floor to ceiling, in drawings. My drawings. Every doodle I'd ever made since I could hold a crayon. Every birthday card. Every terrible comic. In the middle of the room was a desk, a brand new drawing tablet, and a letter. "Your teachers said art isn't a real job. We never believed them. Here are eighteen years of proof that you never stopped. We saved for this the whole time." I'm twenty-two now. I draw for a living. And last week, my parents called me over, because they told me there's a second locked door in the house… and it opens when I turn twenty-five.
